tool.enigma.note.ioc: IoC is the index of coincidence of the whole message decrypted with that setting: about 0.038 for random letters, 0.067 to 0.077 for English or German text. A setting that fits the crib by chance turns the rest into noise; the right one (with the right plugboard) reads as text.
tool.enigma.note.neverItself: A crib can only sit where none of its letters lines up with the same letter of the ciphertext: the reflector sends every letter to a different one, so the Enigma never encrypts a letter to itself. Places that pass this test are only not ruled out; they still have to be checked.
tool.enigma.note.none: No setting of the rotors tried makes this ciphertext decrypt to the crib at that place. Check the crib and its position, the ring settings and the plugboard (a real plugboard hides the crib from this search), or widen the rotors to try.
tool.enigma.note.noneTimedOut: Nothing found before the time limit: the search was cut short, see the note below.
tool.enigma.note.pathLegend: The current enters through the plugboard (Plug), runs through the rotors from right to left, turns round in the reflector (UKW), comes back through the rotors from left to right and leaves through the plugboard to light the Lamp.
tool.enigma.note.plugboard: Honest limit: this search assumes the plugboard you entered (none by default). Wartime traffic used up to ten plugboard pairs, which swap letters before and after the rotors, so the crib no longer lines up and this search finds nothing. Breaking that took Turing's bombe (with Welchman's diagonal board): it ignores the plugboard by following the loops the crib draws between letters, and finds the plugboard afterwards. This search is a first step, for messages without a plugboard or whose plugboard you already know.
tool.enigma.note.reciprocal: Encryption and decryption are the same operation: the reflector makes the machine its own inverse. To decrypt, type the ciphertext into a machine set up exactly as it was for encrypting (same rotors, rings, start positions and plugboard).
tool.enigma.note.ringsFixed: The ring settings are fixed at {rings} for this search. A different ring setting looks like a shifted start position only until a rotor turns its neighbour over; if you do not know the rings, put the crib near the start of the message.
tool.enigma.note.stepsLegend: “Stepped” lists the rotors that turn on that key press, before the current flows (R is the right rotor, M the middle one, L the left one; G is the Greek wheel of the M4, which never turns). A * marks the double step: the middle rotor stood on its notch, so it turns again and takes the left rotor with it.

tool.jwt.error.cannotSign: Cannot sign with "{alg}" here. Use none, HS256, HS384 or HS512.

tool.jwt.error.keyBadJson: The key looks like JSON but does not parse. Paste a JWK or a PEM.

tool.jwt.error.noSignature: This token has no signature part, so there is nothing to crack.
tool.jwt.error.noWebCrypto: WebCrypto is not available here (it needs HTTPS or localhost). HS256/384/512 still work.
tool.jwt.error.notFound: No JWT found. A token is three Base64URL parts joined by dots and starting with "eyJ", e.g. eyJhbGciOi….eyJzdWIi….signature.

tool.jwt.error.signBadJson: The input starts like JSON but does not parse. Check quotes and commas.
tool.jwt.error.signEmpty: Paste a token to re-sign, or JSON like {"user":"admin"}.

tool.jwt.error.signatureNotB64: The signature is not Base64URL ({reason}) Was the token cut short?

tool.jwt.note.emptySecret: The secret is the empty string.

tool.jwt.note.mismatchKey: Signature does NOT match ({alg}) with this key.
tool.jwt.note.mismatchSecret: Signature does NOT match ({alg}) with this secret. Wrong secret, or try "Secret is Base64"; Crack mode tests common weak secrets.
tool.jwt.note.noAlg: The header has no "alg". Servers differ in how they handle that.
